bifrost: springboard/src/bare/input.rs (kernel input devices), springboard/src/media/v4l2.rs (UVC cameras via kernel V4L2), springboard/audiod (audio devices); no app-facing USB API; springboard/sdk/src/usb_device.rs (claim planning, not sent to devices)
summary: IOUSBHost lets apps talk to custom USB devices. BifrOSt gives an app that declares the usb permission raw access to one device the person picked on a permission sheet: the shell opens the usbfs node, applies claim, endpoint and control rules (usb_session) and runs the transfers on a worker, and apps get descriptors, bulk, interrupt and control I/O and attach events through bifrost_app::usb_access. System-driven classes (audio, HID, storage, video, hubs, smart cards) are never offered. Isochronous streaming and a hardware check on Midget remain.

features.feature: Device driver access (claim, configure, descriptors, device requests)
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/usb_device.rs (plan_claim, ClaimPlan), springboard/core/src/usb_claim.rs, springboard/core/src/usb_descriptors.rs, springboard/src/shell/services/usb_access.rs, springboard/sdk/src/usb_access.rs, springboard/core/src/usb_session.rs
features.note: An app can plan a claim (configuration and alternate-setting requests in order, and the pipes the interface opens), and the setup packets and descriptors are encoded and parsed in the inline tests of usb_claim.rs and usb_descriptors.rs. Gap: nothing sends the requests and the sandbox binds no /dev/bus/usb, which needs hardware and a Midget check. Refreshed 2026-10-17: covered by springboard/core/src/usb_claim.rs; tests usb_claim::tests. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): Built the path an app takes: the usb manifest permission, a permission sheet where the person picks one device (Allow Once, Always Allow, Don't Allow), and the shell's usb service, which opens /dev/bus/usb/BBB/DDD itself, reads the descriptors and runs claim, release, alternate setting, reset and control requests through usb_session::Session on a worker thread. No device node enters the sandbox. Interfaces of classes the system drives cannot be claimed. Remaining: needs a device check on Midget. Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-core usb_grants:: usb_session:: hidraw:: and cargo test -p springboard --features desktop-wayland usb_access::; on the device: plug a USB serial adapter (vendor-specific interface) into Midget, run an app that declares `usb` in its manifest and calls usb_access::request from the front window, then usb_access::open and claim(0); the Done events carry the result. Settings > Privacy & Security > App Permissions shows a USB AND HID DEVICES group (screenshot with `bifrost pc midget screen`).

features.feature: Interface, pipe and stream I/O (control, bulk, interrupt, isochronous)
features.note: Wave 4 (theme-14, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No pipe or stream abstraction exposed to apps. Refreshed 2026-10-17: covered by springboard/core/src/usb_pipe.rs; tests usb_pipe::tests. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): Bulk and interrupt reads and writes (4096 bytes a call, 16 in flight, timeouts capped), class and vendor control requests, and clear halt run on the device's worker and finish as Done events; endpoints must belong to a claimed interface in the active alternate setting and match their direction. Isochronous transfers are planned (Session::isochronous_plan) but not sent: they need a URB queue. Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-core usb_grants:: usb_session:: hidraw::; on the device with a USB serial adapter: usb_access::write(handle, 0x02, b"AT\r") then read(handle, 0x81, 64) and see the Done event data.

Wave 4 (theme-14, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Needed for audio and video class devices if apps are to drive them directly. Refreshed 2026-10-17: covered by springboard/core/src/usb_pipe.rs; tests usb_pipe::tests. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): Session::isochronous_plan checks that the endpoint is isochronous and in a claimed interface and returns the frame list (usb_transfer::plan_isochronous). Sending isochronous frames is not built (needs the usbfs URB queue, SUBMITURB and REAPURB, and a device that streams). Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-core usb_grants:: usb_session:: hidraw:: (usb_session::tests::the_isochronous_plan_needs_an_isochronous_endpoint_of_a_claimed_interface); no on-device check until the URB queue exists.

features.feature: Matching and IOServicePlane device and interface properties
features.bifrost: springboard/ui/src/os_services/usb.rs (Matching, Device, DeviceClass, parse_id, parse_code); springboard/sdk/src/os_services.rs; springboard/src/bare/input.rs (device discovery by capability, kept current on hotplug), springboard/core/src/usb_grants.rs, springboard/src/shell/services/usb_access.rs
features.note: Matching by vendor, product, class, interface subclass and protocol, and sysfs identifier parsing, are tested headless in tests/parity_sdk-os-06.rs. Gap: the device monitor does not hand live descriptors to apps, so callers must supply the Device values. Refreshed 2026-10-17: covered by springboard/ui/src/os_services/usb.rs; tests tests/parity_sdk-os-06.rs. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): Matching now runs against live devices: the service reads the bus every second (usb_bus_source), and an app's request filters (vendor, product, class, and for HID usage page and usage) pick which devices the sheet offers. An app sees only devices it was granted, so there is no way to enumerate the bus. No registry-style property tree. Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-core usb_grants:: usb_session:: hidraw:: (usb_grants::tests::a_request_offers_only_eligible_matching_ungranted_devices_up_to_the_limit) and cargo test -p springboard --features desktop-wayland usb_access::; on the device: usb_access::request with a vendor filter offers only that device.

Keyboard and pointer interfaces are recognised from the HID protocol codes and tested headless. Gap: input events still reach apps only through the window system, and no live device list is exposed. Refreshed 2026-10-17: covered by springboard/ui/src/os_services/usb.rs; tests tests/parity_sdk-os-06.rs. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): Keyboards are deliberately not offered to apps: the raw USB path refuses HID interfaces and the HID path refuses keyboards, keypads and security keys (hidraw::protected), so an app cannot log typing. Pointing devices and vendor HID devices reach an app through the hid permission and hidraw reports. Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-core usb_grants:: usb_session:: hidraw:: (hidraw::tests::keyboards_keypads_and_security_keys_are_protected) and cargo test -p springboard --features desktop-wayland usb_access::protected_devices_are_never_offered_and_keyboards_never_opened.

Video streaming interfaces are recognised from the UVC class codes and tested headless. Gap: cameras are still reached through kernel V4L2 in the shell, and apps get no frames from this model. Refreshed 2026-10-17: covered by springboard/ui/src/os_services/usb.rs; tests tests/parity_sdk-os-06.rs. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): Video-class interfaces are protected (usb_grants::protected_class), so raw USB access to a camera is refused; cameras stay behind the camera permission and the shell's capture path. Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-core usb_grants:: usb_session:: hidraw:: (usb_grants::tests::the_system_driven_classes_are_protected_and_vendor_specific_is_not).

Audio streaming interfaces are recognised from the USB audio class codes and tested headless. Gap: audiod does not take a USB endpoint from this model, and apps cannot select one. Refreshed 2026-10-17: covered by springboard/ui/src/os_services/usb.rs; tests tests/parity_sdk-os-06.rs. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): Audio-class interfaces are protected too: an app cannot claim them raw, audiod keeps the endpoint. Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-core usb_grants:: usb_session:: hidraw:: (usb_grants::tests::a_device_is_eligible_when_one_interface_is_not_system_driven).

Wave 5 (w5-iousbhost, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests, now including can_print (a printer interface needs a bulk-out endpoint) and the printer name for a list, tested headless in parity_sdk-complete-45.rs. Not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. The print API does not expose a USB transport. No scanner API exists: most USB scanners use vendor-specific protocols, so scanner support needs per-model drivers and a device. Refreshed 2026-10-17: covered by springboard/core/src/usb_printer.rs; tests usb_printer::tests. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): Printers can be granted to an app (class 7 is not protected): usb_printer::find_printer picks the interface and bulk endpoints from the open reply, device_id_request, port_status_request and soft_reset_request send the class requests, and PrintJob sends the bytes in chunks with short-write handling. System print dialogs still use CUPS. No scanner API (vendor protocols need per-model drivers). Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-app usb_access:: external_accessory:: usb_printer::; on the device with a USB printer or label printer: grant it, claim the printer interface, send a PrintJob.

features.feature: Host controller interface and state machines (hubs, controller, port, endpoint)
features.bifrost: Linux kernel xHCI and USB stack
features.note: Controller-side DriverKit plumbing. On Linux the kernel owns it, and a desktop app has no use for it.

features.feature: Error domain and structures, enumerations, constants
features.note: Apple error and ABI types for the IOKit USB path. No equivalent is needed without the framework.

gaps: No app-facing transport: the claim plan (springboard/sdk/src/usb_device.rs) is not sent and no control, bulk, interrupt or isochronous request reaches a device (IOUSBHostDevice, IOUSBHostInterface, IOUSBHostPipe, IOUSBHostStream).
The app sandbox (springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs) does not bind USB device nodes, so a sandboxed app cannot reach raw USB even if an API existed.
No USB transport for printers (springboard/ui/src/print.rs); scanner sessions are an SDK model (sdk scan_session.rs) with no transport.

Owner decision needed: whether a desktop needs app-level raw USB access at all. The triage note says likely n/a; the framework's stated use cases (cameras, audio, scanners, printers, MIDI, hubs) are mostly covered at the system layer, which leaves custom device drivers as the real gap.
